Honda Activa to Honda Passiva - The Mylapore Story

# Honda Activa to Honda Passiva - The Mylapore Story

### Or Why ISRO and NASA are bidding for Mylapore

[](https://substack.com/@amaruvi)

![Amaruvi Devanathan's avatar](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!Bq_i!,w_36,h_36,c_fill,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F357700fd-8e69-44fa-a5f8-000e6e26808a_1002x1002.jpeg)

There was a time when Mylapore roads merely connected one destination to another.

Today they connect orthopaedic surgeons to new customers.

Progress.

When you were growing up, the only pits we knew were mango pits.

You ate the mango, sucked the seed until your mother threatened legal action, and threw the pit away.

Today every street in Mylapore has more pits than a mango season in Salem.

North Mada Street alone appears to have been shortlisted by NASA as a backup landing site. The Mandaveli Road is filing a PIL against this. It’s crater near Kasturi Malagai is already a landmark.

In fact, if Chandrayaan ever develops a puncture, I strongly suspect ISRO can simply redirect it to Luz Corner.

The terrain is identical.

Possibly rougher.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The greatest achievement of modern civic engineering is that nobody knows whether a hole in the road is:

1.  A pothole.

2.  A Metro excavation.

3.  A sewage repair.

4.  An abandoned archaeological project.

5.  The entrance to Patala Lokam - chance to meet Mahabali Chakravarti.

Every crater arrives without explanation and departs without closure.

Like certain relatives.

You wake up one morning and discover half the street missing.

No notice.

No warning.

No ribbon-cutting ceremony.

Only a barricade leaning drunkenly at forty-five degrees and a handwritten sign saying:

**“Inconvenience is regretted.”**

By whom?

Certainly not by the people who created it.

You could at least have asked the MLA to declare the crater open. At least we could know who the person is. Hmmm…

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Metro project deserves special appreciation.

Most cities build underground rail systems.

Mylapore appears to be conducting a geological excavation of the Earth’s core.

Every week they dig deeper.

Every month they discover another pipe.

Every year they promise completion.

I am now convinced they are searching for buried Chola treasure.

Or perhaps the original filter coffee recipe.

Nothing else explains this enthusiasm for continuous excavation.

Archaeologists at least occasionally find artifacts.

Our contractors only find more cables.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The roads themselves have evolved beyond infrastructure.

They are now interactive experiences.

The Tourism Department should charge tickets.

“Welcome to Mylapore Adventure Park.”

Helmet mandatory.

Spinal alignment optional.

Look at the entrepreneurship of Mylapore bone surgeons. There is a bone and joint clinic next to each pit. One has been pithily named ‘Pit & Pot Hole Clinic’.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Software professionals will immediately understand the situation.

Mylapore roads are a legacy application.

Nobody understands the original architecture.

Every fix creates three new bugs.

Every patch breaks another module.

Every release is rolled back.

The entire system is running on undocumented dependencies and prayers.

The potholes themselves are not defects.

They are “unexpected open-source features.”

Citizens are simply participating in public beta testing.

Every scooter rider is essentially a Quality Assurance engineer.

The difference is that software testers usually survive the test environment.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Last week I attempted to ride from South Mada Street to R.K. Mutt Road.

Google Maps estimated seven minutes.

My suspension contemplated retirement.

My kidneys submitted resignation letters.

At one point my scooter descended into a crater so deep that my GPS recalculated my location as Sri Lanka. I was so certain it should have been Brazil.

When I emerged, I was in a different emotional state.

Possibly a different geological era.

And my late scooter in the Iron Age.

Result : My “Activa” became “Passiva”.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The true architectural masterpieces, however, are the manholes.

Calling them manholes is unfair.

They are kinetic sculptures. Kapali Temple sculptures hang their head in shame looking at them.

The manholes are actually Urban installations.

Experimental hydraulic testing platforms.

Each one rises majestically above road level like a newly crowned emperor.

You approach cautiously.

You calculate trajectory.

You invoke every known deity.

Then THUD.

The vehicle achieves temporary flight.

The passenger experiences involuntary enlightenment.

And the suspension absorbs trauma that would normally require counselling.

These manholes are not covers.

They are entrance examinations. ( not conducted by NTA ).

Only worthy vehicles may proceed.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

One particularly famous manhole near Mylapore Temple has become so elevated that locals use it as a navigational landmark.

“Turn left after the second temple and before the giant concrete volcano.”

Everybody knows which one.

No address required.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Speaking of volcanoes, let us discuss sewage manholes.

These marvels periodically erupt with all the enthusiasm of Mount Vesuvius.

The fragrance alone can dissolve childhood memories.

Somewhere beneath Mylapore, I am convinced there exists a subterranean civilization conducting chemical warfare. ( Don’t let Trump know, Saar ).

Every eruption creates a fresh obstacle course.

Every obstacle course creates fresh devotees.

The cycle of samsara continues.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Carnatic music lovers have suffered particularly.

The roads have become deeply musical.

Every pothole introduces a new tala pattern.

Unfortunately the composition is performed directly upon your vertebrae.

Ride through Mylapore and you experience:

**Adi Thalam for the first hundred metres.**

**Khanda Chapu near the signal.**

**Misra Chapu after the Metro barricade.**

**Complete rhythmic collapse outside the bus stop.**

The vibrations generated by a scooter crossing three consecutive craters produce gamakams previously unknown to musicology.

My retired boss Asuri, a mridangist by hobby, recently told me:

“Why practice korvais ? Just ride around Mylapore for twenty minutes.”

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The December Season has also adapted.

Rasikas no longer walk into Sabhas.

They perform athletics.

Triple jump.

Long jump.

Pole vault.

Obstacle navigation.

Last Margazhi, I witnessed a seventy-three-year-old Mami execute a leap worthy of Olympic qualification merely to reach the entrance of a Sabha.

The concert began with Vathapi Ganapathim.

Her landing concluded in Chatusra Nadai.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Naturally, Mylapore Mamis have opinions.

One Mami informed me:

“I am not stepping out.”

“Why Mami?”

“The road is more unpredictable than my mother-in-law’s mood.”

A powerful statement.

Particularly because the mother-in-law passed away in 1998.

Yet her reputation remains stronger than the Corporation’s.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Last heard, the Election Commission has removed all the households of Ramachandra Iyer Street from its electoral rolls as the street itself was missing. Electricity, Cable TV, Jio, AirTel, BSNL and of late, the Metro Rail have apparently dug it up. Metro Water has complained to the Chennai Corporation that their employees have nowhere to dig as all places are dug wide open.

To assist visitors to Mylapore, I propose a formal crater rating system.

### The Mylapore Crater Index™

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

⭐ One Star Crater  
Minor inconvenience.  
May spill coffee.

⭐⭐ Two Star Crater  
Passenger begins questioning life choices.

⭐⭐⭐ Three Star Crater  
Vehicle emits sounds not covered by warranty.

⭐⭐⭐⭐ Four Star Crater  
Spine relocates slightly to the left.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Five Star Crater  
Entire family discusses selling the vehicle.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Six Star Heritage Crater  
Visible from space.  
Eligible for independent PIN code. (600000)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

One legendary crater near the Metro route deserves special recognition.

School children use it for geography projects.

Birds migrate through it seasonally.

During monsoon, local residents consider applying for fishing licenses.

I understand property tax notices are now being issued separately to the crater itself.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The truly remarkable part is that every road repair lasts approximately the lifespan of a Carnatic concert tiffin token.

Fresh tar appears.

Photographs are taken.

Social media posts emerge.

Citizens experience hope.

Then a week later someone digs it up again.

Apparently road construction now follows the principles of reincarnation.

Nothing ends.

Everything merely returns in another form.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Mylapore residents have become resilient.

We identify craters by family names.

Rangachari Pit, Justice Sundaram Crater, Venkatakrishnan Pothole.. the list goes on.

Of late, during Chief Minister’s birthdays, they are erecting banners near craters.

CM = Crater; MLA = Dug up Manhole; Councillor = Pothole.

We exchange pothole updates like stock tips.

We discuss road conditions with greater seriousness than global geopolitics.

“How is North Mada?”

“Volatile.”

“What about Kutchery Road?”

“High risk.”

“R.K. Mutt Road?”

“Suitable only for trained professionals.”

“Venkatraman Pothole is becoming a crater next week. I see a JCB there”

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Perhaps we are looking at this incorrectly.

Maybe these roads are not broken.

Maybe this is cutting-edge urban innovation - Smart Cities Project probably.

Where else can you simultaneously experience:

- Adventure tourism

- Spine realignment

- Suspension stress testing

- Archaeological exploration

- Religious surrender

- Classical rhythm training

All on a single scooter ride?

Last week Padma Subramaniam rejected a bunch of students who had come for training in Bharatnatyam, for they were already trained in jumping over potholes.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Foreign delegations should be invited immediately.

Let engineers from Germany observe a manhole that is taller than the surrounding road.

Let Japanese transport experts witness a crater capable of swallowing half a sedan.

Let NASA examine North Mada Street before spending billions on lunar simulation facilities.

Let London Tube engineers explore if a crater could be used as a Metro Rail depot.

In Mylapore, the infrastructure already exists. We need to repurpose.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Until then, dear residents of Mylapore, ride carefully.

Carry water.

Carry patience.

Carry insurance.

Carry a backup vertebral column if available.

And when somebody asks why our roads look like satellite images of the Moon, tell them proudly:

“We are not suffering from neglect.”

“We are participating in India’s most ambitious space program - Mylaporeyaan.”

Because, if this pace continues, Mylapore will become the first neighbourhood in Chennai where reaching the grocery store technically qualifies as extraterrestrial travel.

And if we can’t fix the road, let’s at least declare Mylapore a UNESCO-protected crater site.

**A parting note to Mylaporeans** - While navigating the elevated man-hole near Sai Baba Temple.. sorry.. while going to the elevated man-hole via the Sai Baba Temple, perform a pradkshanam to the man-hole, preferably an anga-pradakshanam so that you go home with your vertebral column intact.

Your ‘Activa’ shall remain an ‘Activa’ for ever.
